note: Bundled, opt-in tzatlas rules. Every rule cites a primary source (statute/ordinance/Federal Register/ICC/DOT order or an official standard-time map) and must be ADDITIVE vs default tzdata. Cases tzdata already handles (e.g. Indiana's 1938 Central status, already in America/Indiana/*) do not belong here. See README.md.

rules.name: North Dakota on Central Standard Time, 1946-1966
rules.source: NBS Circular 406, 'Standard Time Throughout the World', Fig. 1 (ICC-defined U.S. standard-time-zone map: most of North Dakota shown in Central time); and U.S. DOT order FR 2010-24376 (29 Sep 2010), recounting the 1929 ICC Central extension and the 1968 DOT order moving ND's Missouri-River counties to Mountain time.
rules.note: North Dakota was in the CENTRAL standard zone and observed no summer DST in 1946-1966, so civil time was CST (-6) year-round. This corrects tzdata on BOTH sides: western ND (America/North_Dakota/{Center,New_Salem,Beulah} and America/Denver) is wrongly Mountain pre-1968, and eastern ND (America/Chicago) is wrongly given Chicago's summer DST (CDT). The southwesternmost corner was actually Mountain in this era (1929 ICC) -- a small fringe kept CST here by choice and flagged, not carved out. War time (1942-02 to 1945-09, when ND was CWT -5) and 1967 (Uniform Time Act, when ND observed DST) are intentionally left to tzdata. bbox is North Dakota's bounding rectangle; negligible overreach along the wiggly Red River into western Minnesota, which was also Central.
